correctness.rationale: The original graph shortest-path definition reduces to clique components at diameter two. The star/triangle partition bijection is directly checked, and yields exact bivariate EGF including one-uncovered exception. In the Poisson assembly, r b'(r)=n, B(r)~n/r, Var(N)~nr and Var(J)=O(n/r). Fourier inversion with Gaussian central arc and exponentially small off-central arcs proves a local probability Θ((nr)^(-1/2)); Chebyshev after conditioning gives J~n/r. Exceptional triangles have logarithmic count at most (2/3)nlog n+O(n), versus covered log count nlog n-nloglog n-O(n). Separate original-shortest-path program exhaustively matches polynomial through n=6 (33856 masks). Finite experiments not used as proof.

value.rationale: This natural graph family has a known smallest maximal GP size near n/2 and largest near n. The complete labeled size enumerator, plus a quantified and proved typical deficit n/log n under uniform maximal-set sampling, distinguishes almost-all behavior from extremal options. The precise log-scale makes the result useful for counting, sampling and comparing constrained configurations rather than merely extending a table.
